problem_framing.primary_problem: How to design and structure software using object-oriented principles
secondary_problems: How to properly use inheritance and composition
How to apply design patterns to solve recurring problems
How to achieve encapsulation and abstraction
How to create maintainable and scalable systems
problem_framing.context: Software design and programming across multiple languages and domains

core_assumptions: Objects are the natural unit of organization in software
Real-world entities can be modeled as objects with state and behavior

layer_1_foundation.name: OOP Fundamentals
layer_1_foundation.description: Basic building blocks of object-oriented systems

layer_2_relationships.name: Object Relationships
layer_2_relationships.description: How objects relate and interact with each other

layer_3_behavior.name: Object Behavior
layer_3_behavior.description: How objects exhibit different behaviors in different contexts

layer_4_design.name: Design Patterns
layer_4_design.description: Proven solutions to recurring design problems

thinking_patterns.description: Breaking complex systems into smaller, single-responsibility objects

thinking_patterns.trigger: When identifying similar objects with variations

thinking_patterns.description: Designing interfaces that allow different implementations
Hiding internal state behind controlled interfaces

potential_biases: Misuse of inheritance for code reuse (composition should be preferred)
Creating god objects with too many responsibilities
key_mental_shifts: From procedural thinking (functions operating on data) to object-oriented thinking (objects combining data and behavior)
From flat structures to hierarchical, modular designs
From monolithic systems to component-based architectures
From 'how to implement' to 'how to model domain'
